newsitem.title: USA: IHOP trims 1996 new restaurant openings.
newsitem.headline: IHOP trims 1996 new restaurant openings.

text.p: IHOP Corp. said Thursday it has scaled down plans to open new International House of Pancakes restaurants this year because of intense competition for low-cost family dining.

The Glendale, Calif.-based company now expects open 65 and 70 restaurants this year, rather than 75 to 80 as previously expected. These include 45 to 50 restaurants developed by the company and about 20 by IHOP's franchisees and area licensees.
IHOP also said same-store sales rose for a fourth consecutive month, by 1.8 percent, in September, compared with a 0.7 percent increase in the year-ago period.

The company attributed the strong performance to a new advertising campaign initiated in May, a new menu that went systemwide in the latter part of 1995, and an improved focus on unit level operations.

IHOP opened 19 restaurants in the third quarter ended Sept. 30, 1996, bringing the total restaurants year-to-date to 42. During the quarter, IHOP franchised 17 restaurants, of which 16 were developed by the company and one by a franchisee.
IHOP has 711 restaurants, including 518 operated by franchisees, 61 by the company and 132 by area licensees. IHOP restaurants are located in 36 states, Canada and Japan.
IHOP's stock fell $3 to $19.75 early on Nasdaq.
